stem.text: The function \( g \) is defined for all real \( x \) by \( g(x) = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{x} (t - 3)e^{t}\,dt \).

parts.prompt: Find \( g'(x) \) and the value of \( x \) at which \( g \) has a critical point.

worked_solution.text: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus the derivative is the integrand at x.
Set the derivative equal to zero; e^x is never zero.

points.criterion: Sets g'(x) = (x - 3)e^x equal to zero, or writes an equivalent equation, to locate the critical point.

parts.prompt: Determine whether \( g \) has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at the critical point found in part (a). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: e^x is positive, so the sign of g'(x) is the sign of x - 3.
worked_solution.latex: g'(x) < 0 \text{ for } x < 3, \quad g'(x) > 0 \text{ for } x > 3

worked_solution.text: g' changes from negative to positive at x = 3, so g has a relative minimum there.

points.criterion: States the sign of g' on each side of x = 3 (negative before, positive after), or the sign of g''(3), explicitly.
Concludes that g has a relative minimum at x = 3, with the conclusion tied to g' changing from negative to positive (or to g''(3) > 0).
